artifacts.summary: Recorded both rulings in claude-refresh.service (new-passes ruling + ConditionPathExists deploy-path ruling), rebuilt a ten-item canonical pass inventory in SKILL.md and refresh.md, and confirmed every acceptance gate green.

completion_data.completion_summary: Settled the unattended-refresh policy by recording both rulings in claude-refresh.service's comment block and implementing ConditionPathExists, then rebuilt skill-refresh/SKILL.md and commands/refresh.md around a from-source-derived ten-pass canonical inventory (correcting both the task description's seven and the research report's nine). All five acceptance gates ran green: both systemd units verify, check-extension-docs.sh reports core PASS, --help matches the documented inventory, and no task-number or .claude/** hand-edit was introduced.

memory_candidates.content: When editing a source-store script under agent-system/extensions/*/scripts/** that check-extension-docs.sh also drift-checks against its deployed .claude/ copy, an edit to the source alone transiently FAILs the 'core' row with 'deployed script content drift' until the deployed tree catches up. Resolve by running `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` (default, non-destructive resync mode) rather than hand-editing .claude/** -- this is the sanctioned deploy/reload mechanism explicitly exempted by source-store-deploy-boundary.md, and it also surfaces a useful post-deploy report of stale consumer repos.

When a task description asserts a specific count of items to inventory (e.g. 'seven passes'), treat that count as a hypothesis to verify, not ground truth -- even an upstream research report's own count can be wrong. Derive the real count by enumerating directly from source (function calls in a script's main(), heading/subsection structure in docs) in a dedicated phase before any downstream phase consumes the inventory; this caught two omitted items (a directory-cleanup operation and a stale-backup-file cleanup step) that both the task description and the research report missed.
